recognize_zh: 中央大細胞有圓形核、細緻顆粒狀染色質，外圍是一圈無顆粒的深藍色細胞質，核周稍淡染，比周圍的髓系細胞和晚期幼紅血球都大，符合原紅血球（proerythroblast）。
features: Large round cell, among the largest in the field
Round central nucleus with finely granular chromatin; nucleoli are indistinct at this resolution
High N:C ratio with a distinct rim of intensely basophilic, agranular cytoplasm
Faint perinuclear clearing (pale zone around the nucleus)
Background marrow with later normoblasts, myelocytes, metamyelocytes and bands
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows maturing granulocytic and erythroid elements, including myelocytes, band forms and late normoblasts with pyknotic nuclei. The central cell is large with a round nucleus, finely granular chromatin and a rim of deeply basophilic, agranular cytoplasm with slight perinuclear clearing. No cytoplasmic granules or Auer rods are present. Findings are consistent with a proerythroblast, the earliest morphologically recognizable erythroid precursor.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts have lighter blue to gray cytoplasm, more open chromatin with prominent nucleoli and may contain azurophilic granules or Auer rods, unlike the intensely basophilic agranular cytoplasm here.
Basophilic normoblasts are smaller with coarser checkerboard chromatin and no nucleoli.
Plasma cells have an eccentric nucleus and a prominent paranuclear hof, whereas this nucleus is central.
Megakaryoblasts often show cytoplasmic blebs and require CD41/CD61, and lymphoma cells lack erythroid maturation; immunophenotyping (CD71, E-cadherin, glycophorin) separates them.
